Virovitica New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Virovitica, Croatia

Not demolished. Virovitica's first Jews arrived from Hungary in the 18th century, though a formal community was only established in the mid-19th century; its synagogue, built in 1863, was among the first in Slavonia, with seats purchased for 300 forints each by its prosperous business-owning members. The community built a bilingual German-Hebrew school in 1875, reaching a peak of 2,854 Jews across the wider area by the century's end. Following WWI, the community suffered riots from returning Austrian army veterans, and the interwar economic crisis hit hard, leaving only 350 Jews by 1940. During the Holocaust, more than 160 were killed and many more deported; in 1942, Croatian nationalists destroyed the synagogue. Virovitica was the birthplace of noted Croatian-Jewish writer Miroslav Feldman (1899–1976), known for psychological dramas with grotesque elements and sharp social critique of provincial life. This new cemetery, established in 1867 by the community's own Hevra Kadisha, holds about 181 graves ranging from 1872 to 1942, with inscriptions in German, Hebrew, Hungarian, and Croatian; the 1991–92 Croatian civil war left visible bullet scars across many of its tombstones.
